title: The periodic table
keyIdea: Elements are arranged by atomic number in rows (periods) and columns (groups). Elements in a group have similar properties.

kid: The periodic table lists every element. Each box shows a symbol and a number, such as 6 for carbon. That number is the atomic number: how many protons each atom has.
Columns are called groups. Elements in the same group behave in similar ways. Rows are called periods. Metals are on the left and in the middle, and non-metals are on the right.
adult: In 1869 Dmitri Mendeleev put the known elements in order. He left gaps for elements no one had found yet and predicted their properties. When gallium and germanium were discovered, his predictions matched.

Patterns run down each group. In Group 1, the alkali metals, reactivity increases as you go down: lithium fizzes in water, while potassium bursts into a lilac flame. Group 0 (also called Group 18) holds the noble gases, which barely react at all.

familyTip: Find a periodic table online and look up five elements you use at home.

practice.prompt: What are the columns of the periodic table called?
practice.explain: Columns are groups; rows are periods.

practice.prompt: An element has atomic number {z}. How many protons are in each of its atoms?
practice.explain: The atomic number is the number of protons, so {z}.

practice.prompt: Where are the metals in the periodic table?
choices: On the left and in the middle
practice.explain: Most elements are metals, filling the left and middle.

practice.prompt: A neutral atom has {z} protons. How many electrons does it have?
practice.explain: A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons: {z}.

practice.prompt: Lithium, sodium and potassium are in Group 1. Which is the most reactive?
practice.explain: Potassium is lowest of the three, so it is most reactive.

pool.prompt: A neutral atom has {z} electrons. What is its atomic number?
pool.hint: Electrons = protons in a neutral atom.
pool.explain: It has {z} protons, so its atomic number is {z}.

pool.prompt: An element has atomic number {z}. How many electrons does a neutral atom of it have?

pool.explain: Elements in a group react in similar ways.

pool.prompt: What did Mendeleev do that made his table so convincing?
choices: He left gaps and predicted elements that were found later
He put the elements in alphabetical order
pool.explain: His gaps predicted elements such as gallium and germanium, which were later found.

pool.prompt: Which group contains the noble gases, which barely react?
pool.explain: The noble gases are in Group 0, also numbered Group 18.

pool.prompt: What is the atomic number of an element?
choices: The number of protons in its atoms
pool.explain: It is the number of protons.

pool.prompt: Which of these is a non-metal?
pool.explain: Sulfur is a non-metal; iron and sodium are metals.
